.social-toolbar {

        .toolbar-divider {
            display: none;
            width: 1px;
            height: 1.25rem;

        }

        /* Right Side on Mobile / Next to Divider on Desktop: Comment & Share Icons */
        .share-comment-group {
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            gap: 0.5rem;
            position: relative;
            margin-left: auto; /* Pushes Comment & Share to the right edge on mobile */
        }

        }

        .toolbar-icon-btn {
            color: #374151;
            border: none;
            padding: 0.5rem;

            display: flex;

            justify-content: center;
            font-size: 20px;

        .toolbar-icon-btn:hover,
        .toolbar-icon-btn.is-active {
            color: #000;
            background-color: #f3f4f6;
        }

        /* Share Dropdown Menu */
        .share-dropdown-menu {
            display: none; /* Hidden by default */

            right: 0; /* Aligns to right edge so it stays inside mobile screen */

            width: 12rem; /* 192px */

            border: 1px solid #e5e7eb;

	</div></p><p>However, essential services such as hospitals, ambulances, fire services, medicine shops and milk supply were exempted from the bandh, a Congress leader said.</p><p>INDIA bloc parties, including the Congress, CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, Forward Bloc, NCP (Sharad Pawar), Samajwadi Party, RJD and JMM, have been observing the 12-hour Odisha bandh since 6 am, demanding repeal of the new mining law, the resignation of state minister Nityananda Gond over “errors” in school textbooks and the alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.</p><p>“We demand a complete rollback of the MMDR (Amendment) Act, resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar for ‘vote chori’ and state minister Nityananda Gond for distributing books with erroneous information among school students,” senior Congress leader Suresh Routray said in Bhubaneswar.</p><p>Adequate security arrangements have been made across the state to avoid any untoward incidents during the protest, said a senior police officer.</p><p>Efforts have been made to ensure that the protests during the bandh take place democratically and peacefully.</p><p>Bhubaneswar-Cuttack Police Commissioner S Dev Dutta Singh said, “Discussions have been held with various stakeholders so that protesters conduct their demonstrations within the ambit of their constitutional rights.” PTI BBM BBM BDC<div id="1133db14-2b87-4ccf-b1c5-8045d99fd647" data-section="1133db14-2b87-4ccf-b1c5-8045d99fd647" class="_ap_apex_ad" data-xpath="#postcontent > p:eq(8)" data-section-id="" data-ap-network="adpTags" style="display: block; clear: both; text-align: center; margin: 10px auto; width: 728px; height: 90px; overflow: hidden;" data-render-time="1795339104652">

<script data-nopdlab="true">
/*for Font resize*/
$('document').ready(function(){
	var cookie = "fontsize";

	var getFontSize = function(){
		var value = parseInt($.cookie(cookie))
	  return  value||20;
	}

	var changeFontSize = function(direction){
	  var newSize = Math.min(24, Math.max(16, getFontSize()+direction))
	  $.cookie(cookie, newSize, {expires: 30, path: '/', domain  : ''});
	  updateFontSize(newSize)
	}
	var updateFontSize = function(fontsize){
	  var style = $('#font_size_style')
	  if(!style.length){
		style = $('<style id="font_size_style">')
		$(document.body).append(style)
	  }
	  style.text(".td-post-content p { font-size: "+fontsize+"px; line-height: "+(fontsize + 10)+"px;}")
	}

	var initFontSize = function(){
	  var fontsize = getFontSize()
	  console.log(fontsize)
	  updateFontSize(fontsize)
	}

	$(document).ready(initFontSize); 

	$('#td-outer-wrap').on( "click", "#up", function() {        
	  changeFontSize(1)
	});

	$('#td-outer-wrap').on( "click", "#down", function() {
	  changeFontSize(-1)
	}); 
});
</script>

.custom-quotes {

}

.custom-quotes::before,
.custom-quotes::after {
	position: absolute;
	z-index: -1;
	display: block;
	width: 3rem;
	height: 4rem;
	content: "";
	z-index: 0;
	font-size: 8rem;
	font-family: Georgia, Times, Garamond, serif;
}

.custom-quotes::before {
	top: 1.5rem;
	left: 0.5rem;
	content: open-quote;
}

.custom-quotes::after {
	bottom: -5rem;
	right: 1rem;
	content: close-quote;
}

.custom-quotes::before,
.custom-quotes::after,
.block-quote h2 {
	text-shadow: -2px 2px #fff, -1.5px 1.5px #fff, -1px 1px #fff, -0.5px 0.5px #fff;
}

	margin-block-end: 1rem;
}

// Dropdown Menu Logic using clean semantic CSS classes
const shareButton = document.getElementById('shareButton');
const shareDropdown = document.getElementById('shareDropdown');
let isDropdownOpen = false;

function toggleDropdown(forceState) {
    isDropdownOpen = forceState !== undefined ? forceState : !isDropdownOpen;
    
    if (isDropdownOpen) {
        shareDropdown.classList.add('is-visible');
        // Small delay to allow display:block to apply before triggering CSS transition
        setTimeout(() => {
            shareDropdown.classList.add('dropdown-enter-active');
        }, 10);
        shareButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
        shareButton.classList.add('is-active');
    } else {
        shareDropdown.classList.remove('dropdown-enter-active');
        shareDropdown.classList.remove('is-visible');
        shareButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
        shareButton.classList.remove('is-active');
    }
}

// Toggle on button click
shareButton.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    e.stopPropagation();
    toggleDropdown();
});

// Close dropdown when clicking outside
document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    if (isDropdownOpen && !shareDropdown.contains(e.target) && e.target !== shareButton) {
        toggleDropdown(false);
    }
});

// Prevent closing when clicking inside the dropdown itself
shareDropdown.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    e.stopPropagation();
});

// Copy Link to Clipboard function
function copyToClipboard() {
    const url = window.location.href;
    const textArea = document.createElement("textarea");
    textArea.value = url;
    textArea.style.position = "fixed";
    document.body.appendChild(textArea);
    textArea.focus();
    textArea.select();
    try {
        document.execCommand('copy');
        showToast('Link copied to clipboard!');
    } catch (err) {
        console.error('Unable to copy link', err);
    }
    document.body.removeChild(textArea);
    toggleDropdown(false);
}

// Toast notification helper
function showToast(message) {
    const toast = document.createElement('div');
    toast.textContent = message;
    toast.className = 'toast-notification';
    document.body.appendChild(toast);
    
    setTimeout(() => {
        toast.style.opacity = '0';
        setTimeout(() => document.body.removeChild(toast), 300);
    }, 3000);

( ( dropdownId ) => {

	function onSelectChange() {
		setTimeout( () => {
			if ( 'escape' === dropdown.dataset.lastkey ) {
				return;
			}
			if ( dropdown.value ) {
				document.location.href = dropdown.value;
			}

	}
	function onKeyUp( event ) {
		if ( 'Escape' === event.key ) {
			dropdown.dataset.lastkey = 'escape';
		} else {
			delete dropdown.dataset.lastkey;
		}
	}
	function onClick() {
		delete dropdown.dataset.lastkey;
	}
	dropdown.addEventListener( 'keyup', onKeyUp );
	dropdown.addEventListener( 'click', onClick );
	dropdown.addEventListener( 'change', onSelectChange );

Resignation of Odisha education minister</h3>The opposition has sought the resignation of School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond over alleged errors in school textbooks.<br><br><div data-size="[[300,250]]" data-loc="2" id="div-gpt-ad-858478132-1-134779476" class="country_specAD2nd"></div><h3>4. Relief for flood victims</h3>The INDIA bloc has also demanded adequate rehabilitation and compensation for people affected by floods in Odisha.<br><br><h2>Odisha Bandh: What's likely to remain closed?</h2>The bandh could affect several parts of daily life, although the extent of disruption will vary by location.<br><br><h3>Schools and colleges</h3>Educational institutions may remain closed or suspend normal activities in areas where the bandh has a strong impact. The INDIA bloc has appealed to educational institutions to suspend normal operations during the shutdown. However, students appearing for examinations are not supposed to be stopped from reaching their examination centres. Parents and students should therefore check directly with their schools or colleges before travelling.<br><br><h3>Shops and markets</h3>Markets, shops and commercial establishments are expected to face disruptions, particularly in areas where protesters are holding demonstrations or picketing. The bandh organisers have asked supporters to persuade shops and businesses to remain closed rather than use force.<br><br><h3>Auto-rickshaws</h3>Auto-rickshaw services could be affected in several areas. The Bhubaneswar Auto-rickshaw Mahasangh has indicated that it does not want to risk operating vehicles during the protest because of concerns about possible disruption.<br><br><h3>Public transport</h3>Transport is expected to be among the services most affected. The INDIA bloc has asked buses, auto-rickshaws, trucks and other commercial vehicles to stay off the roads during the bandh. At the same time, the private bus owners' association had said before the bandh that its services would continue unless a fresh decision was taken. This means passengers could see route-specific cancellations, delays or diversions, even where operators have not formally announced a shutdown.<br><br><h2>Are buses running in Odisha today?</h2>The situation is not uniform. Ama Bus services are expected to operate, but routes may be cancelled or diverted depending on the intensity of protests. Private bus operators had also said they intended to operate normally. However, road blockades could still disrupt services in different parts of the state. People travelling by road should therefore allow extra time and check local transport updates before starting their journey.<br><br><h2>What's open during Odisha Bandh?</h2>Essential and emergency services have been kept outside the bandh.<br><br>These include:<br><br><ul><li>Hospitals and nursing homes</li><li>Clinics and emergency medical centres</li><li>Ambulances, including 108 and 102 services</li><li>Blood banks and diagnostic centres</li><li>Pharmacies and Jan Aushadhi Kendras</li><li>Fire and rescue services</li><li>Emergency police services</li><li>Milk distribution and essential milk supplies</li><li>Emergency electricity and water restoration services</li></ul>The bandh organisers have specifically instructed protesters not to obstruct these services.<br><br><h2>Will government offices remain open?</h2>The Odisha government has asked district administrations to ensure the functioning of government offices and essential services. However, government offices could still see disruptions in places where protests, demonstrations or road blockades take place. The state has deployed police personnel and asked officials to maintain law and order.<br><br><h2>Odisha Bandh: What about petrol pumps?</h2>Petrol pumps and other commercial establishments could be affected by the bandh in some locations. Reports from Bhubaneswar indicate that several commercial establishments and petrol pumps at prominent locations are expected to remain closed. However, this may not apply uniformly across the state.<br><br><h2>Odisha Bandh: What should commuters know?</h2>The biggest impact is expected on road movement. Police have been deployed at sensitive locations, including highways, railway stations and other important points. In Bhubaneswar, around 100 officers and 18 platoons of police force have been deployed to manage the situation, according to the city police. Commuters should avoid unnecessary travel through protest-prone areas and check local traffic updates before leaving home. 			  "articleBody":"Odisha Bandh Today: Odisha is observing a 12-hour statewide bandh today, October 8, after opposition parties under the INDIA bloc called for a shutdown over the amended mining law, alleged errors in school textbooks and concerns surrounding the electoral roll revision. The bandh began at 6 am and is scheduled to continue until 6 pm. The protest is expected to affect road transport, markets, educational institutions and some business establishments across the state. The Odisha government has directed district collectors and police officials to take preventive measures and ensure that essential services continue during the shutdown.Odisha Bandh today: Who is protesting?The bandh has been called by the Odisha units of INDIA bloc parties, led by the Congress. The participating parties include the Congress, CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, Forward Bloc, NCP (Sharad Pawar), Samajwadi Party, RJD and JMM, according to reports.The alliance has appealed to supporters to hold rallies, demonstrations, picketing and sit-ins while keeping emergency services outside the bandh. The Biju Janata Dal (BJD), however, has decided to stay away from the October 8 bandh. The Naveen Patnaik-led party said it would maintain equal distance from the BJP and Congress.Why is Odisha observing a bandh today?The INDIA bloc has raised several demands behind the shutdown.1. Withdrawal of MMDR Amendment ActThe opposition is demanding the withdrawal of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026. The parties have opposed changes to the mining law and raised concerns over the state's rights over its mineral resources.2. Resignation of CEC Gyanesh KumarThe parties are also demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations linked to the Special Intensive Revision, or SIR, of electoral rolls. The issue has become a larger political flashpoint, with opposition parties also holding protests in Delhi.3. Resignation of Odisha education ministerThe opposition has sought the resignation of School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond over alleged errors in school textbooks.4. Relief for flood victimsThe INDIA bloc has also demanded adequate rehabilitation and compensation for people affected by floods in Odisha.Odisha Bandh: What's likely to remain closed?The bandh could affect several parts of daily life, although the extent of disruption will vary by location.Schools and collegesEducational institutions may remain closed or suspend normal activities in areas where the bandh has a strong impact. The INDIA bloc has appealed to educational institutions to suspend normal operations during the shutdown. However, students appearing for examinations are not supposed to be stopped from reaching their examination centres. Parents and students should therefore check directly with their schools or colleges before travelling.Shops and marketsMarkets, shops and commercial establishments are expected to face disruptions, particularly in areas where protesters are holding demonstrations or picketing. The bandh organisers have asked supporters to persuade shops and businesses to remain closed rather than use force.Auto-rickshawsAuto-rickshaw services could be affected in several areas. The Bhubaneswar Auto-rickshaw Mahasangh has indicated that it does not want to risk operating vehicles during the protest because of concerns about possible disruption.Public transportTransport is expected to be among the services most affected. The INDIA bloc has asked buses, auto-rickshaws, trucks and other commercial vehicles to stay off the roads during the bandh. At the same time, the private bus owners' association had said before the bandh that its services would continue unless a fresh decision was taken. This means passengers could see route-specific cancellations, delays or diversions, even where operators have not formally announced a shutdown.Are buses running in Odisha today?The situation is not uniform. Ama Bus services are expected to operate, but routes may be cancelled or diverted depending on the intensity of protests. Private bus operators had also said they intended to operate normally. However, road blockades could still disrupt services in different parts of the state. People travelling by road should therefore allow extra time and check local transport updates before starting their journey.What's open during Odisha Bandh?Essential and emergency services have been kept outside the bandh.These include:Hospitals and nursing homesClinics and emergency medical centresAmbulances, including 108 and 102 servicesBlood banks and diagnostic centresPharmacies and Jan Aushadhi KendrasFire and rescue servicesEmergency police servicesMilk distribution and essential milk suppliesEmergency electricity and water restoration servicesThe bandh organisers have specifically instructed protesters not to obstruct these services.Will government offices remain open?The Odisha government has asked district administrations to ensure the functioning of government offices and essential services. However, government offices could still see disruptions in places where protests, demonstrations or road blockades take place. The state has deployed police personnel and asked officials to maintain law and order.Odisha Bandh: What about petrol pumps?Petrol pumps and other commercial establishments could be affected by the bandh in some locations. Reports from Bhubaneswar indicate that several commercial establishments and petrol pumps at prominent locations are expected to remain closed. However, this may not apply uniformly across the state.Odisha Bandh: What should commuters know?The biggest impact is expected on road movement. Police have been deployed at sensitive locations, including highways, railway stations and other important points. In Bhubaneswar, around 100 officers and 18 platoons of police force have been deployed to manage the situation, according to the city police. Commuters should avoid unnecessary travel through protest-prone areas and check local traffic updates before leaving home. Emergency vehicles, however, are expected to receive free passage.",

            mobileForms.forEach(form => {
                const icon = form.querySelector('.search-icon');
                if (!icon) return;

                icon.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
                    e.preventDefault();
                    // toggle active class
                    form.classList.toggle('active');

                    if (form.classList.contains('active')) {
                        const input = form.querySelector('input');
                        if (input) input.focus();
                    }
                });
            });

            // Close when clicking outside
            document.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
                if (!e.target.closest('.mobile-search')) {
                    document.querySelectorAll('.mobile-search.active')
                        .forEach(f => f.classList.remove('active'));
                }
            });
        });

                    <p id="first-paragraph">
                        </p><blockquote><p><em><b>Synopsis:</b> Sugarcane farmers demanding ₹5,500 a tonne blocked National Highway 48 at Kognoli toll plaza on the Karnataka–Maharashtra border for a second day on Wednesday, disrupting traffic between the two States. Police advised motorists travelling between Pune, Kolhapur and Karnataka to avoid the highway and take alternative routes through Satara, Miraj and Gokak. Farmers’ leader Chunappa Pujeri said talks with Union Ministers Pralhad Joshi and Shivraj Singh Chouhan had produced no concrete decision on cane prices; the farmers are also seeking a minimum sugar price of ₹60 a kg.</em></p></blockquote>
<p>Traffic on National Highway 48 remained disrupted for the second consecutive day on Wednesday, 14 October, as sugarcane farmers continued their blockade at Kognoli toll plaza on the Karnataka–Maharashtra border, demanding ₹5,500 a tonne for sugarcane.</p>
<p>A Belagavi district police officer told South First that the blockade was affecting vehicle movement between the two States. Farmers had also blocked highways at Hirebagewadi and Hattargi in Belagavi district on Tuesday.</p>
<p>Kolhapur Range Inspector General of Police Ranjan Kumar Sharma advised motorists travelling between Pune, Kolhapur and Karnataka to avoid NH-48 until the protests end.</p>
<p>“Farmers’ organisations have been protesting at several toll plazas in Karnataka since this morning, leading to traffic congestion at some locations along NH-48. The situation may continue for some time. I appeal to motorists travelling between Pune, Kolhapur and Karnataka to avoid NH-48 until conditions improve,” Sharma said in a video posted on X.</p>
<p>Police advised motorists undertaking essential travel to use either the Satara–Rahimatpur–Vita–Tasgaon–Miraj–Gokak–Belagavi route or the Satara–Karad–Islampur–Ashta–Miraj–Gokak–Belagavi route. Sharma said traffic and local police were making arrangements along both routes and urged motorists to avoid the affected areas unless necessary.</p>
<p><strong>Also Read: <a href="https://thesouthfirst.com/karnataka/ktaka-sting-op-row-siddaramaiah-sees-character-assassination-bid-claims-innocence/">K’taka sting Op row: Siddaramaiah sees character-assassination bid, claims innocence</a></strong></p>
<h3>Farmers reject Centre’s response</h3>
<p>The farmers are also demanding a minimum selling price of ₹60 a kg for sugar, implementation of the Swaminathan Commission recommendations and government procurement of ethanol produced in Karnataka.</p>
<p>The protests intensified after a meeting between farmer representatives and Union Ministers Pralhad Joshi and Shivraj Singh Chouhan in New Delhi on Monday, 12 October. The Centre said a high-level joint committee would be constituted within a week to examine grievances over sugarcane recovery rates, weighing discrepancies, wastage deductions and other issues.</p>
<p>Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha leader Chunappa Pujeri called the meeting unsuccessful, saying farmers had received no concrete decision on their pricing demands. Joshi described the discussions as constructive and urged farmers to stop blocking roads.</p>
<p>Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar also met Joshi in New Delhi on Monday night to discuss farmers’ grievances.</p>
<p><strong><em>(Edited by Dese Gowda)</em></strong></p>

    <script type="text/javascript">
        // Mobile Menu Toggle
        const mobileMenuBtn = document.getElementById("mobileMenuBtn")
        const mobileMenuOverlay = document.getElementById("mobileMenuOverlay")
        const closeMobileMenu = document.getElementById("closeMobileMenu")

        function openMobileMenu() {
          mobileMenuOverlay.classList.add("active")
          document.body.style.overflow = "hidden"
        }

        function closeMobileMenuHandler() {
          mobileMenuOverlay.classList.remove("active")
          document.body.style.overflow = ""
        }

        if (mobileMenuBtn) {
          mobileMenuBtn.addEventListener("click", openMobileMenu)
        }

        if (closeMobileMenu) {
          closeMobileMenu.addEventListener("click", closeMobileMenuHandler)
        }

        if (mobileMenuOverlay) {
          mobileMenuOverlay.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
            if (e.target === mobileMenuOverlay) {
              closeMobileMenuHandler()
            }
          })
        }
    </script>
